summary:
SOL 60: Red Horizon is a free, browser-based 3D Mars survival and planetary science simulation powered by real NASA mission data. Running natively in any standard web browser with zero downloads or high-end hardware, the game puts you in the boots of a TIF-7 astronaut landing in Gale Crater with one mission: survive, conduct real science, transmit a message to Earth, and reach the summit of Olympus Mons to escape Mars.

Before launch, you have 60 seconds and a strict credit budget to choose your gear—forcing real aerospace engineering trade-offs because you cannot afford everything. On the surface, every decision is shaped by genuine Martian hazards: thin air, extreme cold, dust storms, martian earthquakes, solar flares, and a rover battery that never holds enough power. To survive and advance, you solve interactive science and engineering puzzles: matching mineral spectra to real orbiter data, routing scarce power across rover subsystems, aligning solar panels, and finding Earth’s signal.

The simulation’s weather, gravity, seismic activity, and terrain follow published NASA datasets from Curiosity, Perseverance, InSight, MOLA, and the Mars Fact Sheet, while a live telemetry overlay displays each real-time metric next to its NASA source. By turning abstract planetary data into lived intuition, SOL 60: Red Horizon helps students and the public feel why exploring Mars is so hard—and why it matters.
details:
WHAT IT IS

SOL 60: Red Horizon is a browser based 3D Mars survival, science, and low gravity mountaineering game built on real NASA data. Open the link on any laptop, desktop, or tablet; nothing to install. Need a fast overview? Click "60 Second Judge Path" on the title screen for an automated one minute tour of the full mission.

HOW IT WORKS

  1. Pre Launch Bunker: You have 60 seconds and 100 credits to buy gear from 9 items worth 208 credits total, including an O2 scrubber, seismic anchors, rover fast charger, spectrometer, MMRTG power core, and plant chamber. You can afford less than half, forcing real engineering trade offs that shape your entire run.
  2. Ares 7 Descent: A narrated landing sequence plunges you into Gale Crater and introduces the hazards of Mars.
  3. Field Operations: Explore, repair shelters, and drive your rover while managing energy in watt hours (Wh). Driving, slopes, headlights, and freezing temperatures drain your battery; recharge by aiming solar arrays at the Sun, brushing off storm dust, or linking to repaired power stations.
  4. Science & Engineering Puzzles (15–45s): Solve rapid, authentic spaceflight challenges: balancing airlock pressure and temperature, routing scarce power across subsystems, matching rock spectra to real MRO CRISM mineral bands, triangulating Earth’s signal, and aligning solar panels.
  5. Dynamic Hazards: Survive rolling dust storm cloud fronts, solar flares, a final super storm, and three stage marsquakes (warning rumble, dislodged boulders, and rockfall at Mars’s real 3.72 m/s² gravity).
  6. Olympus Mons Ascent: Leave the rover behind to scale sheer volcanic cliffs, managing grip, pitons, oxygen reserves, and 0.38 g low gravity leaps, to rescue the stranded crew at the summit.
  7. Telemetry Debrief: Review your mission score with every performance metric linked directly to its NASA dataset.

REAL NASA DATA

Empirical Environment: Temperature, pressure, wind, UV, and gravity follow published ranges from Curiosity (REMS), Perseverance (MEDA), and the NSSDC Mars Fact Sheet. Marsquakes draw from InSight SEIS data, terrain from MOLA topography, and minerals from MRO CRISM spectra. Live Data Overlay (Press N): Toggle a real time HUD comparing every simulated value against its verified NASA range, complete with clickable source citations. Honest Scale Disclosure: Gale Crater and Olympus Mons sit roughly 5,340 km apart on Mars. An explicit in game notice explains that both landmarks are combined into one playable region so players can experience basin and summit extremes in a single mission.

BENEFITS AND IMPACT

Felt Science: Turns abstract planetary numbers into real stakes: players feel how thin air, cold, dust, and tight watt hour budgets constrain actual Mars missions. Scientific Transparency: Every metric is cited, and every gameplay simplification is openly explained. Classroom Ready: Free, zero install, and built to run smoothly on everyday school laptops and tablets.

ACCESSIBILITY

Multi Sensory Alerts: Full captions for all radio and audio cues, paired with visual Morse beacons so critical information never relies on sound alone. Inclusive Controls: Reduced motion mode, on screen touch controls, fully rebindable keys, and zero reliance on a middle mouse button.

TOOLS AND TECHNOLOGY

Stack: React 19, Three.js, Vite, Tailwind CSS, and Web Audio API, hosted on GitHub Pages. 100% Procedural Assets: Every 3D model, texture, and sound effect is generated in code with zero external asset files, enabling instant loading even on slow school networks. Automated Verification: Validated by 29 Vitest tests covering game logic, collision physics, and NASA data accuracy.

WHAT MAKES IT CREATIVE

It fuses resource survival, low gravity mountaineering, and real planetary science into a single cohesive mission. Instead of memorizing Mars facts, players make high stakes engineering decisions under the exact physical limits astronauts and rovers face.

WHAT WE CONSIDERED

Strict fidelity to NASA datasets, honest disclosure of geographic scale, inclusive sensory and motor accessibility, instant zero asset loading, and smooth performance on standard laptops and tablets.
